detail.longDescription: I have a .NET service which connects to AWS S3 with access key and secret. It has ability to update itself with new binary. At some point in time, I've changed my access keys and removed old ones from account, and of course updated my service beforehand with new binary with new access keys. However due to a scripting error, my service got overwritten by an older version which uses old keys. Now of course AWS is complaining about invalid access keys when it tries to connect. I need to be able to temporarily make AWS ignore the old access keys and let it connect anyways, so I can update it once more. I have full access on the AWS account. I tried making the S3 bucket public, which lets anonymous access, but still doesn't let the service connect due to invalid key. I don't have physical access to the station with the service atm. Is there a workaround to this? This is for my personal use and it's OK if I need to make bucket public temporarily.
